biography:
Stella 'StarStrider' Sterling grew up in a family of asteroid miners who dreamed of something more than scraping minerals from rocks. Every night, her father would point out different stars and tell her stories about what might be waiting in the systems beyond their isolated outpost—ancient civilizations, strange phenomena, treasures and wonders that no one had ever seen. Stella made it her mission to see those things herself. She signed on with a exploration vessel at eighteen, worked her way up from navigator to captain, and eventually earned enough to buy her own ship. The nickname 'StarStrider' started as a joke about her tendency to treat interstellar travel like a walk in the park, but it became her legend as she spent more time in uncharted space than in settled systems, discovering more jump points and anomalies than any other living pilot. Her navigational charts are highly prized by the Explorers Guild, though she freely shares the information with anyone interested—believing that knowledge grows when it's shared.

StarStrider speaks with the warm, enthusiastic tones of someone who still gets excited about space travel even after decades of exploration. She has the friendly, informal accent of someone who's spent too much time around spacers from all walks of life, and her speech is filled with cosmic metaphors, navigational references, and genuine wonder at the beauty of the universe. She treats every expedition like an adventure and has a habit of turning routine observations into poetic declarations about the grandeur of space. When discovering a new anomaly, she sounds like she's unveiling a masterpiece: 'Look at that! Would you just look at that? That's not just a nebula, that's the universe painting with light and gas across a thousand light-years. You see those colors? That's ionized hydrogen and helium dancing with stellar winds, putting on a show that's been running for millions of years just so we could see it today. I never get tired of this—never. This right here, this is why I do what I do. Not for the credits or the fame, but for moments like this when the universe shows you something beautiful.'
name: Stella 'StarStrider' Sterling
